newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Tajik rebels take seven more hostages, U.N. says.
newsitem.headline: Tajik rebels take seven more hostages, U.N. says.

text.p: Two international Red Cross staff and five journalists were taken hostage by Tajik rebels on Wednesday in the same area where the same group seized five U.N. personnel on Tuesday, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said.

The two employees of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) were a Briton and a local staff member, he said. The journalists were three Russians -- working for NTV (Russian Independent Television), Itar-Tass and Interfax -- and two Tajiks.
On Tuesday the same rebel group seized two U.N. observers from Switzerland and one each from Austria and Ukraine, together with their Tajik intrepreter.
Eckhard said the Austrian was ill and that Tuesday's incident occurred while he was being taken to a hospital.
He said all the hostages were taken by armed followers of Rizvon Saidov, who once fought for the former Soviet republic's Islamic opposition against the secular government but later switched sides.
Last December, Saidov's group took 23 people hostage, including seven U.N. observers, to demand the release of his brother and three other people. All the hostages were later released.

Tens of thousands of people have been killed in a four-year civil war between the government and Islamist guerrillas. About 45 U.N. military observers are stationed in the country where the Russian-led Commonwealth of Independent States has a much larger peacekeeping force.
After Tuesday's incident, the United Nations said the hostage-takers were demanding safe passage for their members into Tajikistan from Afghanistan, where many anti-goverenment guerrillas are based.
The United Nations has demanded the immediate freeing of all the hostages.
